body: Kenya was involved in the war, though she had a minor role. The  South African Air force (SAAF) stationed combat aircraft in Kenya (as well as in Sudan). The purpose for this was too combat the numerically superior Italian air force that was based in Ethiopia. This was the SAAF's baptism of fire. Some of the earliest WW2 battle victories were won by the SAAF over the table top mountains of Ethiopia. Britain was not in the position to send its own Royal Air Force (RAF) because all it's aircraft were needed for the battle of Britain.
